authority: Explicit curated source references; proposed questions, not human acceptance.

claims.quote: The local fixture serves fixed, already verified PR #1 snapshot bytes at review commit 0484a4b76128c3ed302a6a8d6e0343bfe03cece5 with manifest and SHA-256. It rejects missing resources, incorrect digests and forged unexpected content against a trusted revision/digest anchor before invoking Lisp. One verified read-back passes 31 native TMDM/CXTM assertions covering the known assignment, ten identified evidence entries, reification, source Associations/Roles and source references.
- The fixed fixture comes from review-candidate PR #1 commit `0484a4b76128c3ed302a6a8d6e0343bfe03cece5`; it is not a claim of a merged or deployed snapshot.

The observed `dreyeck.ch` HEAD (`573fe37611a61d984260ebf43c797f7534211bdd`) has no independently loadable DMX MCP runtime. This ports the necessary closure from the verified repair `f512aa847eab05cc2bdf2e78ef0bd1b516a11926`, without merging historical `hauptsache` or changing the separate ISO MCP work.

- Journal correctness and any repair/redesign, state migration or Journal-related DMX Topic cleanup are a **separate investigation Topic and subsequent [work item #7](https://github.com/RalfBarkow/hyperdoc/issues/7)**. Retain only dependencies required by the existing MCP contract. Retaining code and passing fixtures are not Journal-correctness proof.

marks.head: f512aa847eab05cc2bdf2e78ef0bd1b516a11926
marks.label: Reported cold-load failure fingerprint
marks.quote: A fresh `hyperdoc/mcp` image fails resource discovery because it calls `HYPERDOC::JSON-ARRAY-ELEMENTS`, defined only in the unrelated FedWiki slice. A real local HTTP backend reproduces the exact recorded remote response: 214 octets, SHA-256 `4c3cbe31dd2b9f4c489472d172fa90f11e9f144871f1a90f339caa2cbc415df0`, JSON-RPC -32099 and `id:false` for request 2. The matching exception is identified; the running production Git revision remains unknown because no operator deployment record was provided.

marks.head: f512aa847eab05cc2bdf2e78ef0bd1b516a11926
marks.label: Deployed package identity and staging
marks.quote: The operator must identify the deployed source/package and authentication configuration, build/test against that actual pinned environment, review transport timeouts/response limits and preserved write gates in staging, and separately authorize any package activation/restart. This patch does not prove the production backend payload is otherwise valid after the missing-helper exception is removed. Broader historical load warnings/workflows are not claimed repaired; no full suite, live write or production read-back was run.

marks.head: 4ef218a6d273e17091f4ee541965a01ae53d39fc
marks.label: State preservation and later activation unresolved
marks.quote: The user has confirmed the intended public Common Workspace migration contract. The **installed package/source revision, actual resolved Journal directory/recovery behavior and free host disk/inodes remain unverified**. No replacement is recommended until package identity and state preservation are established; source retention does not settle Journal correctness. The operator runbook first captures the installed release metadata, ExecStart and configuration, checks capacity and retains rollback closures; it then describes an exact pinned candidate and MCP-only deployment/rollback through the existing operator-owned `/etc/nixos` setup. The executable-name change requires an explicit ExecStart adaptation: changing only the historical module's package option would be invalid.
